title: Planar energetics do not determine twin persistence in nanocrystalline aluminium
summary: Two learned potentials that reproduce similar planar slip energetics predicted markedly different retained twin coverage (64% versus 14%) from the same precursor under identical loading. The analysis identifies moving-core forces, local traction orientation, and asynchronous partial-slip fronts as determinants that planar energetic descriptors miss. The paper benchmarks Al-QP against five existing models on published DFT data and uses paired first-principles defect calculations to check local forces and energy margins. The result is computational; no experimental confirmation is claimed.
ai_technology: A MACE-based machine-learned interatomic potential (Al-QP), trained on strain-coupled fault, twin, and interface configurations, enabled atomistic simulations of twin formation and persistence in nanocrystalline aluminium.
